cell_type_model: human ADPKD cyst epithelial cells; mouse and human vascular smooth-muscle systems
assay_or_perturbation: recombinant or endogenous periostin; alpha-V integrin blocking antibodies; FAK-inhibitor/FRNK and migration or proliferation assays
relation_type: periostin binds/uses alpha-V integrin complexes including alpha-V-beta-5 and supports ILK or FAK-dependent cellular responses
pathway_branch: ITGAV_ITGB5–ILK/FAK–GSK3B/beta-catenin or adhesion-migration branch
limitations: The ADPKD study reports alpha-V-integrin dependence and ILK/beta-catenin-associated proliferation, while the vascular study supports alpha-V-beta-5 participation in migration but emphasizes alpha-V-beta-3. This is not SCI receiver-cell evidence and does not assign a terminal TF or prove a single alpha-V-beta-5 stoichiometry in every model.

cell_type_model: periostin and PTK7 developmental/ECM or Wnt-related systems
assay_or_perturbation: Exact-pair PubMed, PMC, publisher, and receptor-family searches; comparator periostin-integrin and PTK7 pathway studies
relation_type: no exact Postn-PTK7 binding, activation, receptor-proximal relay, or pair-specific functional assay established
pathway_branch: periostin integrin specificity; PTK7 co-receptor boundary
limitations: Periostin-integrin evidence and PTK7 Wnt/cell-polarity evidence were not transferred to the exact Postn-PTK7 pair. No direct molecular interaction or downstream relay was assigned.

cell_type_model: pancreatic-polypeptide and alpha2A-adrenergic receptor pharmacology systems
assay_or_perturbation: Exact-pair PubMed, PMC, publisher, and GPCR-family searches
relation_type: no exact Ppy-Adra2a binding, activation, receptor-proximal relay, or pair-specific function established
pathway_branch: PP-family Y-receptor specificity; adrenergic-receptor boundary
limitations: Pancreatic polypeptide family pharmacology was not used to infer adrenergic-receptor activation. No exact pair evidence was located.

cell_type_model: PP-family peptides and orphan-GPCR deorphanization systems
assay_or_perturbation: Exact-pair PubMed, PMC, publisher, and orphan-GPCR searches
relation_type: no exact Ppy-Gpr83 binding, activation, receptor-proximal relay, or pair-specific function established
pathway_branch: PP-family Y-receptor specificity; GPR83 orphan/deorphanization boundary
limitations: PEN-family or other orphan-GPCR ligand evidence was not transferred to Ppy-Gpr83. No downstream pathway or TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: PP-family peptide and group-III metabotropic glutamate receptor systems
assay_or_perturbation: Exact-pair PubMed, PMC, publisher, and GPCR-family searches
relation_type: no exact Ppy-Grm7 binding, activation, receptor-proximal relay, or pair-specific function established
pathway_branch: PP-family Y-receptor specificity; GRM7 ligand-family boundary
limitations: Metabotropic glutamate receptor signaling and PP-family Y-receptor pharmacology were kept separate. No exact pair evidence was located.

cell_type_model: PP-family peptide and melatonin-receptor pharmacology systems
assay_or_perturbation: Exact-pair PubMed, PMC, publisher, and GPCR-family searches
relation_type: no exact Ppy-Mtnr1a binding, activation, receptor-proximal relay, or pair-specific function established
pathway_branch: PP-family Y-receptor specificity; melatonin-receptor boundary
limitations: Melatonin-receptor signaling and PP-family pharmacology were not treated as interchangeable. No exact pair evidence was located.

cell_type_model: cloned human Y1 receptor in COS cells; Y1/Y4 receptor-expressing cell and rat-brain binding systems
assay_or_perturbation: competition binding and receptor-expression assays; peptide displacement of Y1/Y4 radioligands
relation_type: PP shows little or very low affinity at Y1R relative to NPY/PYY; no qualifying PP-evoked Y1 second-messenger experiment was established
pathway_branch: PP–NPY1R low-affinity binding boundary; canonical Y1 Gi/o branch not assigned
limitations: The primary Y1 pharmacology places PP below NPY/PYY and the Y1/Y4 study reports little PP affinity at Y1. This supports a bounded binding-only record, not a receptor-proximal relay or terminal TF.

cell_type_model: cloned human hippocampal Y2 receptor expressed in heterologous cells
assay_or_perturbation: 125I-PYY competition binding and expression cloning
relation_type: PP weakly displaces ligand at Y2R (pKi < 6) compared with PYY and NPY; no qualifying PP-evoked Y2 activation assay was established
pathway_branch: PP–NPY2R low-affinity competition boundary; Y2 Gi/o relay not assigned
limitations: The exact primary receptor-cloning study supports only weak PP competition at Y2R. It does not justify assigning a functional PP-Y2 relay from the stronger NPY/PYY Y2 evidence.

cell_type_model: cloned human Y5 receptor in COS-7 cells; live-cell Y5 ligand-mapping systems
assay_or_perturbation: radioligand competition binding; photo-crosslinking, alanine scanning, and receptor/ligand mutagenesis
relation_type: PP binds Y5R with lower affinity than NPY/PYY and participates in mapped ligand-receptor recognition; no exact PP-triggered downstream relay was retained
pathway_branch: PP–NPY5R binding; Y5 Gi/o branch remains unassigned for this exact ligand
limitations: Y5 studies support natural PP recognition but do not provide a matched pair-specific relay endpoint sufficient for Module21A. Affinity and activation vary by peptide and assay context.

cell_type_model: human ErbB2-overexpressing breast-cancer cells; T47D breast-cancer cells
assay_or_perturbation: prolactin neutralization, dominant-negative JAK2/ERBB2/Ras, kinase inhibitors, phosphoprotein and reporter assays
relation_type: PRL/PRLR signaling transactivates ERBB2 phosphorylation and Grb2–Ras–MAPK signaling in breast-cancer models
pathway_branch: PRLR–JAK2–ERBB2–Grb2/Ras–ERK cross-talk
limitations: The evidence is receptor cross-talk, not direct PRL binding to ERBB2. It is human tumor-cell comparator evidence and does not establish an SCI-cell relay or a universal PRL-to-ERBB2 mechanism.

cell_type_model: yeast, COS-7, mouse-brain laminin-receptor fractions, and neuronal/non-neuronal cell systems
assay_or_perturbation: yeast two-hybrid, mapping, overlay, co-immunoprecipitation, cell-surface interaction, and inhibitor perturbation
relation_type: PrP binds the RPSA/37-67-kDa laminin-receptor precursor/mature laminin-receptor system; no intracellular relay was established
pathway_branch: PrP–RPSA/LRP-LR binding and trafficking boundary
limitations: RPSA is multifunctional and the 37-kDa/67-kDa laminin-receptor nomenclature reflects processing/maturation states. This record supports physical association/uptake context only, not a direct TF or canonical intracellular relay.

cell_type_model: Doppel-expressing transfected cells and in-vivo-derived tissues
assay_or_perturbation: yeast two-hybrid, deletion mapping, immunoprecipitation, and immunoblot validation
relation_type: Doppel binds full-length 37-kDa laminin-receptor precursor RPSA/LRP; no receptor-proximal intracellular relay was established
pathway_branch: Doppel–RPSA/LRP binding; PrP and Doppel binding domains are not interchangeable
limitations: The study validates a physical Doppel–LRP interaction but does not establish a signaling receptor function, downstream pathway, or SCI relevance. RPSA mature/precursor state remains explicit.

cell_type_model: purified human Mac-1 alpha-M I-domain and protein-C peptide-library systems
assay_or_perturbation: cellulose-bound peptide-library binding and phage-display motif analysis
relation_type: protein-C-derived peptides contain Mac-1/ITGAM recognition motifs; full-length PROC-to-alpha-M-beta-2 cellular binding or relay was not established
pathway_branch: protein-C peptide–Mac-1 I-domain binding; full-length PROC state boundary
limitations: The source tests peptides derived from protein C rather than a complete native PROC ligand-receptor assay. APC/EPCR and Mac-1 pathway literature was not transferred to an exact full-length PROC–ITGAM relay.

cell_type_model: HUVEC and recombinant Tie2 systems
assay_or_perturbation: Biacore, co-immunoprecipitation, solid-phase binding, Tie2 phosphorylation, barrier assays, and EPCR/PAR1 blocking
relation_type: activated protein C binds and activates Tie2/TEK, but native inactive PROC was not tested as the exact ligand state
pathway_branch: APC–TEK direct agonism; PROC zymogen versus APC state boundary
limitations: The primary study is strong for activated protein C, not for unprocessed PROC. It supports an activation-state boundary and a possible TEK relay only after PROC-to-APC conversion; no exact native PROC–TEK edge is promoted.

cell_type_model: purified protein C, thrombin, thrombomodulin domains, and endothelial-surface complexes
assay_or_perturbation: kinetic, mutagenesis, structural/biochemical, and thrombin–thrombomodulin activation assays
relation_type: thrombomodulin accelerates thrombin-mediated activation of protein C; a standalone direct PROC–THBD ligand-receptor edge was not isolated
pathway_branch: thrombin–THBD–PROC activation complex; EPCR/APC signaling kept separate
limitations: This is cofactor-mediated zymogen activation, not evidence that thrombomodulin independently acts as a signaling receptor for PROC. EPCR and APC-PAR1/Tie2 signaling were not assigned to the inactive PROC–THBD pair.

cell_type_model: HBE/A549/HEK293 epithelial cells; human astrocytoma 1321N1 cells; LNCaP cells
assay_or_perturbation: recombinant human anionic trypsin/PRSS2, calcium mobilization, receptor desensitization, RhoA, and PAR-activating-peptide assays
relation_type: PRSS2/anionic trypsin can cleave/activate PAR1 in receptor- and cell-context-dependent assays and drive calcium or RhoA signaling
pathway_branch: PRSS2–PAR1/F2R–G-protein–Ca2+/RhoA/MAPK branch
limitations: Trypsin-2 activity depends on protease concentration, receptor expression, and cell type; PAR1 is classically thrombin-biased. No SCI receiver weighting or terminal TF is assigned.

cell_type_model: HBE/A549/HEK293 epithelial cells and broader PAR2 assay systems
assay_or_perturbation: recombinant human anionic trypsin/PRSS2, calcium mobilization, PAR2 desensitization, and protease-receptor pharmacology
relation_type: PRSS2/anionic trypsin cleaves and activates PAR2, producing receptor-dependent calcium and downstream PLC/MAPK/Rho signaling
pathway_branch: PRSS2–PAR2/F2RL1–Gq/Gi/G12/13–PLC-Ca2+/MAPK/Rho branch
limitations: The primary isoform study supports PRSS2 activity in epithelial assays; broader pathway descriptions include trypsin-family and non-PRSS2 proteases. No SCI-specific branch weight or terminal TF is assigned.

cell_type_model: mouse platelets and human PAR assay systems
assay_or_perturbation: PAR3-null/PAR4-null platelet experiments; recombinant trypsin isoform and exact-pair searches
relation_type: no qualifying direct PRSS2-PAR3 activation was established; trypsin-induced platelet shape change can be PAR-independent and PAR3 is primarily a thrombin/cofactor context
pathway_branch: PAR3/F2RL2 thrombin-specificity boundary; trypsin-independent platelet signaling
limitations: Trypsin effects in platelets do not establish PAR3 activation, and Doppel-RPSA evidence is unrelated despite the shared search space. No PRSS2-F2RL2 relay was assigned.

cell_type_model: human epithelial/astrocytoma PAR systems; human platelets
assay_or_perturbation: recombinant pancreatic trypsin isoforms, calcium signaling/desensitization, platelet flow cytometry, calcium mobilization, and cleavage assays
relation_type: trypsin-family proteases including anionic trypsin can activate PAR4/F2RL3 in context-dependent assays; recent platelet work directly demonstrates trypsin-mediated PAR4 cleavage and Gq/G12/13 signaling
pathway_branch: PRSS2–PAR4/F2RL3–Gq/G12/13–platelet activation branch
limitations: The older isoform study did not focus on PAR4, while the newer platelet study uses trypsin rather than isolating PRSS2. The exact PRSS2-PAR4 assignment is therefore medium and context-bound; no SCI relay or terminal TF is assigned.

cell_type_model: trypsin/protease and epithelial polarity systems
assay_or_perturbation: Exact-pair PubMed, PMC, publisher, and protease-activated-receptor searches
relation_type: no exact PRSS2-PARD3 binding, activation, receptor-proximal relay, or pair-specific function established
pathway_branch: PAR receptor specificity; PARD3 polarity-scaffold boundary
limitations: PARD3 is a polarity scaffold, not a canonical PAR receptor. PAR1/2/4 evidence was not transferred to PRSS2-PARD3.

cell_type_model: LNCaP prostate-cancer cells; endocrine-resistant breast-cancer cells
assay_or_perturbation: prosaposin or saposin-C treatment, antiandrogen, pertussis-toxin, MAPK/PI3K inhibitors, AR phosphorylation, AR recruitment, and androgen-response reporters
relation_type: prosaposin/saposin C increases AR expression, phosphorylation, nuclear recruitment, and androgen-response reporter activity without evidence of direct PSAP-AR binding
pathway_branch: PSAP/saposin-C–Gi/MAPK/PI3K–AR functional activation
limitations: This is downstream transcription-factor/function evidence, not a direct PSAP-AR molecular interaction and not a canonical membrane-receptor relay. Cell-type and endocrine-resistance context are essential; no terminal TF handoff is made.

cell_type_model: prosaposin/GPR37-family and CELSR1 planar-cell-polarity systems
assay_or_perturbation: Exact-pair PubMed, PMC, publisher, and receptor-family searches
relation_type: no exact Psap-Celsr1 binding, activation, receptor-proximal relay, or pair-specific function established
pathway_branch: prosaposin GPR37/GPR37L1 specificity; CELSR1 adhesion/PCP boundary
limitations: Prosaposin evidence for GPR37/GPR37L1 and CELSR1 developmental signaling were kept separate. No exact pair evidence was located.

cell_type_model: mouse fibroblasts/cortical neurons and recombinant or secreted prosaposin uptake systems
assay_or_perturbation: 125I-prosaposin uptake, LRP/LRP1-deficient or blocking conditions, lysosomal-trafficking and endocytosis assays
relation_type: LRP1 mediates substantial prosaposin uptake and lysosomal delivery; no canonical receptor-proximal signaling branch was established for the exact pair
pathway_branch: PSAP–LRP1 endocytic trafficking/scavenger branch
limitations: The evidence supports receptor-mediated uptake/trafficking rather than a classical G-protein or kinase relay. PSAP–PGRN complex trafficking and LRP1-mediated uptake should not be interpreted as proof of a direct PSAP-LRP1 signaling interaction.

cell_type_model: human U251MG cells; PS1-deficient mouse embryonic fibroblasts; biochemical gamma-secretase systems
assay_or_perturbation: TPA/mechanical-scraping induction, gamma-secretase inhibitors, PS1/PS2 knockout or deficiency, and CD44 intracellular-domain cleavage assays
relation_type: PSEN1-dependent gamma-secretase cleaves CD44 and liberates a signaling intracellular domain; this is enzyme-substrate processing, not ligand-receptor binding
pathway_branch: PSEN1/gamma-secretase–CD44 intramembrane cleavage–CD44 ICD signaling
limitations: The primary studies establish CD44 processing and signaling potential, not a secreted-ligand receptor edge. The exact gamma-secretase complex composition, stimulus dependence, and downstream nuclear partner were not assigned beyond the measured CD44 ICD event.

cell_type_model: PS1/PS2-deficient fibroblasts; gamma-secretase assembly and early secretory-pathway systems
assay_or_perturbation: PS1 rescue, pulse-chase maturation, co-localization, inhibitor-affinity isolation, RNA interference, and complex-assembly assays
relation_type: PSEN1 associates with and is required for NCSTN maturation/assembly in the gamma-secretase complex; no ligand-receptor activation or downstream pair-specific relay was established
pathway_branch: PSEN1–NCSTN gamma-secretase assembly/trafficking complex
limitations: This is a receptor/protease-complex component relationship rather than a ligand-receptor edge. NCSTN maturation and gamma-secretase assembly must not be converted into a secreted-signal relay or TF assignment.
